telegramBot.finding: Native keys and signatures must not move into the Telegram bot; no native signing surface exists.

site.finding: No bounded server-to-native signing request bridge or customer handoff exists.

miniApp.finding: The deployed TON Connect send flow delegates signing to an external wallet and is not native signing.

admin.finding: Operators must not sign with user-local keys; no native signing control exists.

api.finding: Checkout-only E5 modules describe synthetic fail-closed boundary and consent records, but expose no deployed HTTP bridge, persistence or durable replay ledger.

native.finding: Rust core and UniFFI validate an offline Bitcoin Signet preview and hard-code signing/action false; there is no mobile shell, device key lifecycle, authenticator, signature or broadcast.

positiveControls: The Rust scaffold forbids unsafe code, pins toolchain/dependencies and performs no I/O, storage, key, signing or network operation.
Preview validation is Signet-only, bounds inputs/outputs/expiry and derives fees from inputs.
Rust and Python contracts explicitly keep signing, authenticator verification and production-action flags false.
blockers: No device key generation, derivation, hardware wrapping, zeroization, signing or broadcast implementation exists.
No iOS or Android shell, Secure Enclave/Keystore integration, local biometric verification or platform attestation exists.
No durable single-use signing-request ledger, expiry/reconciliation transport or server-to-native bridge exists.
Recovery and trusted-chain/UTXO verification remain design-only; Python synthetic TST contracts and Rust Bitcoin Signet preview are not an end-to-end protocol.
No tracked provenance, reproducible signed mobile build, SBOM, store release or deployed native artifact exists.
